question: Who was the leader that defeated Krishnadevaraya of Vijayanagara in the Battle of Raichur?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Adil Shah of Bijapur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Battle of Raichur** was fought between the forces of **Krishnadevaraya of the Vijayanagara Empire** and **Ismail Adil Shah of Bijapur** in 1520.
 
• **Adil Shah of Bijapur** belonged to the **Adil Shahi dynasty**, which ruled the Sultanate of Bijapur in the Deccan region of India.
 
• The battle was primarily over the control of the **Raichur Doab**, a fertile region situated between the rivers **Tungabhadra and Krishna**.
 
• Although Krishnadevaraya initially achieved a major victory in this battle and captured the Raichur fort, the region later fell into the hands of the **Deccan Sultanates**, including Bijapur.
 
• The battle is significant in Indian history as it demonstrated the use of **advanced artillery** by the Adil Shahi forces, which played a critical role in their success.
 
• **Adil Shah of Bijapur** was known for his military strategies and his ability to form alliances with other Deccan Sultanates to counter the Vijayanagara Empire.
 
• The conflict marked the increasing pressure on the Vijayanagara Empire from the **Deccan Sultanates**, which eventually led to the empire's decline in the later years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Alauddin Khilji**__

 __
 
• **Alauddin Khilji** was a ruler of the **Khilji dynasty** of the Delhi Sultanate, famous for his military campaigns and administrative reforms.
 
• He was known for his successful campaigns in **Rajasthan, Gujarat, and South India**, but he was not directly involved in the Battle of Raichur.
 
• Alauddin Khilji’s reign is remembered for his attempt to control prices through a **market regulation system**.
 
 
 
• **Ahmed Shah Bahmani**__
 __
 
• **Ahmed Shah Bahmani** was a ruler of the **Bahmani Sultanate**, one of the early Muslim kingdoms in the Deccan.
 
• He is known for his administrative reforms and for shifting the Bahmani capital to **Bidar**.
 
• However, he did not play a role in the Battle of Raichur, as it occurred after the Bahmani Sultanate had splintered into smaller Deccan Sultanates, including Bijapur.
 
 
 
• **Ibrahim Lodi**__
 
 
• **Ibrahim Lodi** was the last ruler of the **Lodi dynasty** of the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• He is most famously associated with the **First Battle of Panipat (1526)**, where he was defeated by Babur, leading to the foundation of the Mughal Empire in India.
 
• Ibrahim Lodi was not involved in the Deccan conflicts or the Battle of Raichur.
